# Review — hammurabi-laws-42-51 (§42–51, Col. XII 63 – XIV 66)

## Pass 1 (2026-10-12)

Checked: every glyph against Harper's Plates XIX–XXII (PDF 253, 255, 257, 259), read in zoomed crops line by line, with Harper's List of Signs (PDF 385) for BURU₁₄; every Sumerogram's `val` and `say`; line division (144 lines, XII 63–67, XIII 1–73, XIV 1–66, in order, every line's content matching packet.md); `col`/`line` on every unit = its first stele line; `ln`+`p` only on each law's first unit (§42–51, ten laws); every `reading` reconstructs exactly from its glyphs' `tr` (scripted, 0 mismatches); every grammatical label in the notes; `l` word by word; `l` ↔ `i`; register and consistency with hammurabi-laws-1-10, -11-25, -26-41 and conventions.md.

Harper's own 1904 translation (in the source PDF, PD) was read as a sense check on his readings only.

### Changes (unit · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

1. U6 (§44, XIII 32) · n · **high** · The note presented Harper's "ten GUR per ten GAN" as the reading without saying it is superseded. Harper reads both corner-wedges as the numeral ten; the field-measure notation as now understood counts bur-units with that wedge before the field-sign, so the line means "one bur" and the rent is ten kor per bur (ten times Harper's rate). The honesty rule (Harper as base, modern understanding flagged) applies. · Note rewritten: keeps Harper's reading and translation as the base, states the later reading plainly, and says which is now accepted. Glyphs/`l`/`i` left on Harper.
2. U8 (§45, XIII 43) · n · **medium** · Grammatical claim wrong: "the grammar fits either … (the god) carried off the produce." bi-ib-bu-lum ends in nominative -um, so it is the subject of itbal; Harper's "produce" would need it as object, which the case ending does not support. · Sentence replaced with the case-based argument; flood reading kept.
3. U11 (§47, XIII 62) · n · **medium** · Wrong cross-reference: the earlier (=…) carver's-slip corrections are i-pa-ad-da-ri(=ar)-šu at §32 and il-te-di(=ḳi) at §34 (hammurabi-laws-26-41), not "§25 and §32". · Changed to "§32 and §34".
4. U13 (§47, XIII 67) · n · **medium** · Wrong cross-reference: innaddin occurs at §29 and §32 (innaddiššumma at §28). · Changed to "(§29, §32)".
5. U13 (§47, XIII 66) · n · **medium** · Honesty: ir-ri-su-ma is read as the noun irrissu "his tenant"; Harper reads the same signs as a verb (his "He would cultivate it": erēšum + -šu). The note did not give Harper's reading alongside ours. · One sentence added giving Harper's verbal reading and saying the spelling allows both.
6. U4 (§44) · morph (MU 3{kam}) · **medium** · Lemma "3-years" is an invented key, inconsistent with the published "3-kam" lemma for the identical writing MU 3{kam} (§30). · Lemma set to "3-kam"; gloss kept as the cardinal-duration sense ("for three years"). Glosser: broaden the existing 3-kam entry (it says only "the 3rd") under `__broaden__`.
7. U11 (§47) · i · **medium** · "did not earn his living from it" drifts from the note and `l` (mānaḫātišu … lā ilqû "his outlay/upkeep he did not get"); it also echoes Harper's "has not gained a maintenance". · Now "because he did not get back his outlay in the previous year".
8. U9 (§46) · l · **low** · `u lū … u lū` is "either … or" (the note says so) but `l` read "or for halves or for a-third". · "either for halves or for a-third".
9. U9 (§46) · i · **low** · The dash-parenthesis "— or he leased the field …" made the sharecrop clause read as an alternative to non-receipt of rent, when (as the note says) it explains why no rent was received. · "If he has not yet received the rent for his field, having leased it out either for half or for a third of the crop,".
10. U4 (§44) · n · **low** · Typo "ahšu" (h for ḫ). · "aḫšu".

Totals: high 1 · medium 6 · low 3 (10 changes).

### Plate confirmations (no change needed)
- A.ŠÀ (two signs) on every eqlum line; XIII 6 A.ŠÀ followed by AM (eqlam, phonetic complement) — confirmed. XIV 35, 52 A.ŠÀ-ma confirmed.
- ŠE alone for šeʾum everywhere; ŠE.GIŠ.Ì three signs at XIV 22, 25, 31, 33, 47, 49, 59 — confirmed.
- KÙ.BABBAR, DAM.GÀR (XIV 19 etc.), GÚN (XIII 36, 39, 47), {d}IM (XIII 42, XIV 3), KI.KAL (XIII 18), MU + three verticals + KAM (XIII 19), corner-wedge + GAN₂ + E and corner-wedge + ŠE + GUR (XIII 32–33), BURU₁₄ (XIII 68, XIV 33), KA = pî (XIV 64) — confirmed.
- AZ (lion with ZA inside) in i-ma-aḫ-ḫa-aṣ XIII 13, 27 and u-up-pa-as XIII 65 — confirmed.
- XIII 62: LU sign where QU is expected — confirmed (il-LU-u); Harper's (=ḳu) correction kept.
- XIV 11 [li]: the sign is drawn hatched (damaged) on Plate XXI — Harper's restoration bracket correct.
- XIV 40 and XIV 63: the same KU sign in both il-ḳu-u — confirmed; the plain k in Harper's XIV 63 transliteration is a printing slip, as the U24 note says.
- XIV 4 ir-ta-ḫi-iṣ: TA on the plate (no ṭ).
- XIII 6: plain MA in šum-ma; no reflection of a mark on the plate.

### New signs (new-signs.md) — all three confirmed
- MAR — CUNEIFORM SIGN MAR (U+12225 𒈥): plate XIII 28, second sign of i-mar-ra-ar, matches.
- UZ3 — CUNEIFORM SIGN UZ3 (U+1235A 𒍚): plate XIII 57, the goat-sign between ZU and ZU, matches; no plain "UZ" exists in Unicode (checked).
- BURU14 — CUNEIFORM SIGN EN TIMES GAN2 TENU (U+12099 𒂙): plate XIII 68 and XIV 33 show Harper's List of Signs no. 19 "ebûru" (PDF 385) form, matches.
All three names resolved with `unicodedata.lookup`. Not added to the glossary (per instructions).

### Findings considered and refused
- `tr` writes ḳ (iḳ, ḳi, ḳu) where hammurabi-laws-1-10/-11-25 write q/qi₂. Refused: the latest published part, hammurabi-laws-26-41 (which conventions.md says wins), writes il-te-ḳi, ḳi-iš-ti, iš-ta-ra-aḳ. Cross-part normalization is a QUESTIONS.md matter, not this part's.
- `ù` (U3) for Harper's printed u "and": the model part does the same; the plate shows the Ù sign. Kept.
- MU 3{kam} said šalaš šanātim here vs šattam šalaštam in §30. Kept: §30 is an ordinal "the third year", here ana … "for three years" is a duration; the note flags the spoken form as reconstruction.
- GAN₂.E `val` "būrim" and the U `tr` "10" follow Harper; not changed to the later reading — sole-source rule keeps Harper as base, the note now flags it (change 1).
- u-up-pa-as `tr` "as" (AZ): Harper prints as; AZ carries az/as/aṣ. The verb is uncertain and flagged; no reason to normalize.
- e-bi-ši-im `tr` "bi" said epēšim: same practice as the model (ud-da-ab-bi-ir → uddappir).
- iqbišum morph "-šu" for the dative -šum: the model glosses innaddiššum the same way.
- Remembered English: checked every `i`. "the loss is the tenant's", "at the going rate", "according to the king's schedule", "soak his tablet" are built from the grammar and not distinctive; no echo found apart from change 7. Harper's "according to agreement" is not used (we say "in the agreed proportion", with apšitûm flagged).
- U0 "you will meet it again at §49" (uštabši XIV 32) — correct. U14 note's ibašši + -ma — correct. U16 uraṭṭab D-stem of raṭābum — correct. U23 išu defective verb — correct. U15 šeʾum nominative subject — correct. U10 ibbaššû N-stem + subjunctive — correct.
- XIII 18 "KI.KAL." full stop not carried over: Harper's punctuation, not a sign.

### Unresolved
- q/ḳ notation differs between the published parts (1-10, 11-25 use q; 26-41 and this part use ḳ). Suggest a QUESTIONS.md entry for a normalizing pass; not changed here.
- The glossary entry "3-kam" needs broadening for the duration sense (glosser, pass 2 check).

Re-verified after edits: units.json parses; 25 units; 144 stele lines in exact order and content against packet.md; col/line correct on every unit; ln+p on the first unit of each of §42–51 only; every reading reconstructs from glyph tr (0 mismatches).

## Pass 2 (2026-10-12) — gloss.json and a second read of units.json

Checked: every gloss.json entry (41 new + 6 `__broaden__`) against units.json — lemma string identical to the morph lemma, forms cited occur in the part or are dictionary forms, grammar labels, sense against this part's notes, uncertainty flags, generality; each `__broaden__` value begins with the exact merged entry (computed with r3lib.merged_inline_glossary, publication order) + " · ". Then units.json re-read for note grammar and l ↔ i.

### Changes (unit · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

1. U0, U18 (§42, §49) · n, morph, gloss.json `bašûm-Št` · **high** · Misnamed stem, carried from the draft into the glossary: uš-tab-ši (uštabši) is the Š-stem PERFECT of bašûm (Š prefix uš- + perfect infix -ta-, like imtaḫar), not an Št-stem. An Št present would be uštabaššī; the line context (a past condition) wants the perfect. · Morph lemma → `bašûm-Š` in both words; notes now say "causative Š-stem, perfect (the -ta- after the stem prefix, as in imtaḫar)"; gloss key renamed `bašûm-Š` with the perfect labelled.
2. U6 (§44) · `say` of both "10" words, gloss.json `10` · **medium** · Number said "ešer", the form used with a feminine noun; Akkadian 3–10 take the opposite gender, and kurrum/būrum are masculine, so ešret. The gloss also cited "10 GAN.E ‘ten bur’" as fact after pass 1 flagged that reading as superseded. · say → ešret (marked "(?)" in the gloss, as house rule for reconstructed numbers); gloss rewritten general to the numeral (polarity explained; notes that before a field-measure the wedge may count bur-units, see §44).
3. U4 (§44) · `say` of MU 3{kam}, n, morph gloss, gloss.json `__broaden__` 3-kam · **medium** · "šalaš" lacks the long vowel of the masculine-noun form šalāš (with šanātum, fem., the count takes the masc. form šalāš). · šalaš → šalāš everywhere in this part (say, note, morph gloss, broaden entry). Broaden value still begins with the exact old entry.
4. U4 (§44) · n, gloss.json `nidûtum` · **medium** · Honesty: Harper's nidûtum for KI.KAL given without the modern reading. · Note and gloss now add: later dictionaries read the logogram kankallum "hard, uncultivated land". `val`/say left on Harper (sole-source base).
5. gloss.json `apāsum-D` · **medium** · The suspect item. The lemma string does match units.json; the D-stem label is Harper's own (glossary "APASU, II, 1" = his notation for the D/Piel), and u-up-pa-as as uppas is a regular D present 3 sg. But the entry stated "to object, interfere" without separating Harper's sense from the contextual guess. · Kept key and stem; gloss rewritten: "D-stem (Harper's apāsum II,1), a rare verb of uncertain meaning … sense from context; Harper ‘interfere’". Not renamed: no PD lexical aid in the repository gives a different lemma, and renaming would need a units.json change for no gain.
6. gloss.json `waṣûm-Š`, `šakākum`, `erēšum-N` · **low** · Pinned to this line's form with the chained -ma translated into the gloss ("ušēṣīma … and", "išakkakma … and", "innerišma … and"). · Rewritten with the bare forms (ušēṣi, išakkak, inneriš) and general senses.
7. gloss.json `irrišum` · **low** · Parenthesis "(irriš-šu; …)" said the assimilation backwards for a reader. · "(irriš + -šu; Harper reads the same spelling as a verb, ‘he shall cultivate it’)".
8. U20, U24 (§49, §51) · l · **low** · `l` rendered ša kaspišu "for his-silver"; the literal layer should show ša "of". · "grain of his-silver", "of his-silver and his-interest"; `i` keeps "for".

Totals: high 1 · medium 4 · low 3 (8 changes).

### Glossary entries confirmed (no change)
irrišūtum, šiprum, epēšum, itûm, maḫāṣum, teptītum, aḫum, petûm, rebûm (rebûtim, fem. of rebûm — fine as lemma), marārum, būrum (Harper's GAN, flagged), kurrum, madādum, raḫāṣum, bibbulum (uncertain, Harper "produce" beside "flood"), bitiqtum, mišlum, apšitûm (uncertain, Harper's own "(?)"), zâzum, aššum, maḫrûm, mānaḫtum, ebūrum, ḫubullum, raṭābum-D, ṣibtum, epšētum, šamaššammū, esēpum, eršum, maḫīrum, ṣimdatum. mayyārum (uncertain, both senses) — confirmed, only re-saved. Broaden entries nadûm, tabālum, bēlum, šaluštum, pûm: each starts with the exact merged entry; the additions fit this part's use.

### Findings considered and refused
- Rename `apāsum-D` to another lemma: refused (see change 5) — matches units.json and Harper's lexicon; uncertainty is now explicit.
- bēlum broaden: the oldest parts (prologue, litany) have bare "lord"; the check was against the merged glossary in publication order (1-10/11-25/26-41 override with "owner, lord: …"), so the prefix is correct.
- `10` lemma as a bare numeral string: consistent with published "1", "2" lemmas (hammurabi-laws-11-25).
- ṣibassu "its interest" (gloss) vs morph "-šu his/him": the -šu gloss is the house one; "its" is right in context. Kept.
- ešret vs ešer for the U6 first wedge, if read as "one bur": the spoken form stays on Harper's reading (ten), marked (?).
- Second read of units.json: other note grammar labels confirmed (imtaḫar, G perfect, described as "perfect (-ta- infix)" — correct; ittadi perfect; ibbaššû N + subjunctive; inneriš N; ukannūšu D; uraṭṭab D; turrim D infinitive; erišma/esip/tabal imperatives; išu defective). l ↔ i agree in sense and force throughout.

### Unresolved
- q/ḳ notation across parts (from pass 1) — still for QUESTIONS.md.
- The spoken forms of numbers (ešret, šalāš šanātim) are reconstructions; flagged "(?)" as house rule requires.
